scope: Three authored handlers and predeclared additional input cases. No production bug, held-out bug-discovery or general correctness claim.
baseline: Run the same original handler serially, round-robin and with one seeded random schedule. Report their actual verdicts; do not attribute scheduler enumeration to Meta.
success: At least one completed original-code probe violates the fixed contract, and a model-generated patch has no violation on the checked input/schedule set.
retention: Retain incomplete and failed investigations, including invalid probes and failed patches. No automatic paid transport retry; no repeated investigation to select a nicer result.
limits: QuickJS JavaScript with a simulated asynchronous store. No real HTTP/database/OS scheduling, network faults, arbitrary Node modules or universal concurrency verification. A finite passed sweep proves only the recorded conditions.
